title: Cyber: open L8
points: Use the separate four-bus DC model and its supplied measurement data.
Your task: distinguish a residual alarm from evidence about the true state.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: The four-bus model has three non-slack voltage angles and eight measurements. It is not an AC estimator, malware detector or sensor-authentication system. Synthetic truth is available only for the offline classroom comparison.
caption: Teaching diagram of the model or check used at this notebook step.

title: Read residual and state error separately
points: J measures consistency between readings and the fitted model.
State error compares the estimate with known synthetic truth; an operator does not get that truth.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: The chi-square threshold is about 15.086272 for five residual degrees of freedom at a 1% significance level. This calibration depends on the stated linear model and noise assumptions. A small J does not establish that the measurements are authentic.
caption: Teaching diagram of the model or check used at this notebook step.

title: Run L8: compare two attack patterns
points: Run the whole L8 cell with its default scale list.
Compare isolated bias with coordinated Hc in both the table and plots.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: This cell runs fresh weighted-least-squares calculations. The coordinated counterexample assumes knowledge of the linear measurement matrix and access to the modeled unprotected channels. It is a declared defensive teaching model, not evidence of an incident at a utility.

title: Read your two plots together
points: Left: residual J and the alarm threshold. Right: offline state error.
Follow the coordinated curve across both panels before interpreting a quiet alarm.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: The left plot uses a symmetric-log scale. The right plot compares the estimate with known synthetic truth. As the coordinated shift grows, the residual stays unchanged while the state error increases. These plots answer different questions; they do not express the same quantity in different units.
caption: Actual executed notebook output; source cell classroom-023. Fresh numerical calculation unless explicitly marked archived.

title: At scale 1, what does the alarm miss?
points: Isolated bias: J about 277.50, so the residual alarm is True.
Coordinated Hc: J about 3.92, no alarm, but offline state error is about 0.02678 rad.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: The diagram is a simple scalar illustration of coordinated consistency, not the numerical eight-measurement system. Read the numerical values from L8. A larger false-data shift need not increase the residual when the shift lies in the modeled measurement subspace.
caption: Teaching diagram of the model or check used at this notebook step.

title: Exercise 3: add a small isolated bias
points: Add .10 to ATTACK_SCALES. Predict, then rerun L8.
At scale 0.10, read J, the alarm flag and the offline state error.
Does “no alarm” mean the reading is correct? Use the two panels to explain.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: Allow one minute to predict, two minutes to edit and run, and one minute to report. For isolated bias at scale 0.10, J is about 10.143237, below the 15.086272 threshold. The alarm is False despite nonzero state error. The coordinated residual stays about 3.920222. This added scale remains within the notebook's plot limits.

title: Debrief: a quiet alarm is not proof of truth
points: At scale 0.10, the isolated-bias residual is about 10.14, below the 15.09 threshold.
A threshold can miss a small inconsistency. Coordinated corruption creates a different limitation.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: Separate the two mechanisms. A small isolated bias can stay below a statistical threshold. A coordinated Hc shift can preserve residual consistency by construction. Neither result establishes trusted telemetry. The state-error curve uses offline synthetic truth, not an input available to an online detector.

title: Reset the sweep before recovery
points: Restore the original ATTACK_SCALES list and rerun L8.
Next, L9 uses a fixed trusted-recovery fixture, not the scale you edited.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L8; cell classroom-023; four-bus DC fixture.
note: Explain the boundary before comparing the recovery output. Changing ATTACK_SCALES changes the residual and state-error sweep. It does not change the fixed recovery scenario held inside the demo object.

title: L9 is a fixed recovery example
points: The same supplied recovery case is checked with and without trusted replacement channels.
Its control value does not track your L8 sweep-scale edit.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: The helper uses the fixed run_wls_demo recovery fixture. The cyber object holds both the sweep results and this shared fixed demo. The comparison tests the trust premise under controlled conditions; it is not a controller reacting continuously to each plotted scale.

title: Where do the trusted readings come from?
points: The fixture assumes three independent angle readings are trustworthy.
Neither the residual test nor a language-model explanation authenticates them.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: Three protected angle readings determine three unknown angles, leaving zero residual degrees of freedom. A zero residual in this exactly determined system provides no new detection guarantee. The trust premise must be justified outside this numerical example.
caption: Teaching diagram of the model or check used at this notebook step.

title: Run L9: compare HOLD with PROPOSE
points: Run the full L9 cell, including its assertions.
Read status before comparing the returned injection or offline violation count.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: The two calls use the same fixed fixture and change only protected_available. Without the trusted channels, the result is HOLD. With the assumed trusted set, it is PROPOSE. A proposal is neither an acknowledgment nor a dispatch command.

title: Read the two decision states
points: No trusted replacement channels: HOLD, with no proposed injection.
Trusted channels assumed: PROPOSE, u about 0.121694 p.u., zero offline toy-model violations.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: Read the condition column together with the returned state. The PROPOSE outcome depends on the supplied trust assumption and fixed model. The recovery record keeps dispatch=False. It does not use the equipment_dispatch field from the separate L12 readback example.
caption: Actual executed notebook output; source cell classroom-026. Fresh numerical calculation unless explicitly marked archived.

title: Check the numerical correction
points: The QP minimizes effort while enforcing the declared branch limits and 0.01 p.u. margin.
Predicted flow12 is 0.17000; offline actual is about 0.17046, below the 0.18000 rating.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: The flexible injection is u=0.1216936673 p.u., balanced by the reference bus. The offline actual flow is an audit against synthetic truth for this fixed case. It does not guarantee unmodeled AC behavior or trustworthy field telemetry.
caption: Teaching diagram of the model or check used at this notebook step.

title: Trace what caused the improvement
points: Independent trusted information supplies a usable estimate; the constrained solver supplies the action.
The explanation must preserve those conditions and the remaining need for review.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: Do not attribute recovered information or numerical feasibility to confident prose. The workflow can coordinate the estimator, constrained correction and evidence checks. It cannot invent an independent trusted measurement source.
caption: Teaching diagram of the model or check used at this notebook step.

title: Agent request, tool result, operator decision
points: Agent role: request the allowed estimator/control tool and explain its returned conditions.
Operator role: resolve the trust premise and review the bounded proposal through the authorized process.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: The default classroom calls are deterministic Python functions. The archived model explanations shown in L10 belong to a separate historical study. A real agent implementation would need to bind an allowed request to these tools. This default route makes no new language-model decisions.

title: Cyber checkpoint: state the condition behind PROPOSE
points: Report the measurement-trust assumption, model, proposed u and failed or passed checks.
If independent trusted information is unavailable, retain HOLD and name the missing evidence.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L9; cell classroom-026; fixed trusted-recovery fixture.
note: Ask pairs to state the outcome and its condition in the same sentence. For example: 'The fixture proposes u when the supplied trusted channels are available.' Do not say: 'The AI proved that the telemetry is safe.'
